content.title: Profile lifecycle on Android: Java <-> native bridge
content.description: Same init/storage/deletion path as the desktop ProfileImpl walkthrough, but crossing into Java. On Android, ProfileManager::UnloadProfile() is disabled (#if !IS_ANDROID), so the Java-visible Profile wrapper is instead created/destroyed alongside the native Profile object itself.

notes.text: Java entry point: ProfileManager.getLastUsedRegularProfile() calls into native via JNI to fetch the wrapped regular Profile. See profile_lifecycle_android_sequence.umlsync for the full Java <-> native sequence this walkthrough covers — creation, the onProfileAdded notification, and the two-step destruction handshake (onProfileWillBeDestroyed then onNativeDestroyed).

JNI bridge: JNI_ProfileManager_GetLastUsedRegularProfile calls the native ProfileManager::GetLastUsedProfile() (the same profile_manager.cc/profile_impl.cc creation path already toured on desktop) and returns its Java wrapper.
Every native Profile (ProfileImpl) constructs its Java wrapper right in its own constructor by calling InitJavaObject().
InitJavaObject() calls Java_Profile_Constructor, creating the Java-side Profile object and handing it the native pointer.
Java-side storage: the Java Profile object just holds the native pointer in mNativeProfile — there's no separate Java registry map, it's a 1:1 wrapper per native Profile.
ProfileManagerAndroid observes the native ProfileManager and forwards profile creation to Java via Java_ProfileManager_onProfileAdded.
On the Java side, onProfileAdded() marks ProfileManager as initialized and fans the creation event out to registered Java Observers.
Deletion trigger (Android's substitute for the disabled UnloadProfile): MaybeSendDestroyedNotification() calls NotifyJavaOnProfileWillBeDestroyed() before the native object starts tearing down.
NotifyJavaOnProfileWillBeDestroyed() calls Java_Profile_onProfileWillBeDestroyed while the native Profile is still fully valid.
notifyWillBeDestroyed() — invoked from the @CalledByNative onProfileWillBeDestroyed() below — calls ProfileManager.onProfileDestroyed(this), fanning the pre-destruction event out to Java Observers.
The native Profile destructor runs — same ~ProfileImpl() teardown as on desktop — and additionally calls DestroyJavaObject() to invalidate the Java wrapper.
DestroyJavaObject() calls Java_Profile_onNativeDestroyed, the final native-to-Java call for this Profile.
onNativeDestroyed() zeroes out mNativeProfile so the Java wrapper can no longer touch the (now-destroyed) native object.
Bonus: for off-the-record profiles, Java can explicitly request destruction via destroyWhenAppropriate() — regular profiles are CHECK'd out here since they stay owned by the native ProfileManager.
